findings.reason: the section should ask for the reproducing branch inside `_commitless_raw_field`/`_COMMITLESS_ROLES` to be repaired, not for a declaration parser and a complete-time form that already ship.
findings.text: §2 asks for a read-only run to be allowed `commits: none (reason)` and to promote, but that machinery already exists and already has the raw-field parser the section would otherwise duplicate: `_declares_absent_commits` (promotion_evidence.py:490) reads the declaration before the parenthesis, `_commitless_raw_field` (:758) reads the raw line only for `_COMMITLESS_ROLES = {"review", "investigate"}` (:506), `_opens_with_an_absence_word` (:535) enforces the word boundary, and `--no-commit` already exists on `crew complete` (reckon/crew_run_commands.py:3256). The observed refusal therefore is a defect inside a narrower branch — most likely the role gate at :780 or the citation refusal at :1101 — not a missing feature.

findings.reason: the plan should describe extending the rubric-selects-completeness rule that exists, rather than introducing a second claims check beside reckon/crew/review_records.py:378-412.
findings.text: §3 asks for a claims review record to pass without the six text scores, but the claims rubric and the score exemption already exist: `CLAIMS_RUBRIC = "claims"` (review.py:382-393) is composed and parsed (review.py:1061, :1303) and the completeness check already exempts one non-scored rubric at review.py:972-976 (`_review_record_rubric(record) != FIGURE_REVIEW_RUBRIC`). The section's real change is to make that predicate a set of verdict-per-item rubrics rather than one hard-coded name.

findings.reason: the section sends a worker to build a duty pass that is already built, when the work is finding which precondition keeps the existing composer from firing.
findings.text: §4 asks that a delivered brief-carried run with no plan owe and receive a review, but both halves already exist: `_review_reads_a_report` (recovery_review_subject.py:432-451) already classifies a brief-carried node that committed nothing as a claims review, and `_claims_review_done_when` (:453) already composes that review's brief. §4 therefore is a classification defect — a brief-only delivered run not reaching `promotable`/`scoring` in reckon/crew/recovery_review_dispatch.py's duty input — not a new dispatch path.

findings.reason: the section should name the decode-before-filter defect that reproduces at the base revision, because as written it reads as a new read path beside an index that already filters.
findings.text: §5 asks for a one-plan read that costs nothing for other plans' runs, but `read_records(project, root, plan=...)` already implements a plan selection and already applies `activity_since` inside the index query (ledger.py:1710-1790, `aggregate_filter`/`document_filter`), while `with_figures=False` already avoids the whole-history figure pass. The measurable defect to reproduce is the post-filter at :3812 running after the full decode, which is a filter-pushdown to the existing query rather than a new read.

findings.reason: the plan should extend the index query with a plan predicate rather than add a parallel filtered read, and should name both post-filter sites so one pass repairs them.
findings.text: §5 would place a per-plan read beside the run index that already owns filtered reads: `RunStore._indexed_records`/`records` (reckon/run_store.py:649, :781) and `ledger._index_payload` (reckon/ledger.py:1710) are the single owner of decoding and filtering run documents, and `activity_since` is pushed into SQL there. A new reader that filters by plan after `read_records`'s decode duplicates that owner, and the census of the same defect is two sites today: ledger.py:3812 (`read_records`) and ledger.py:3880 (`review_scores`) both post-filter `plan` after the rows are decoded.

findings.reason: the section should state that the promotion writes the existing `base_sha` beside the existing `no_commit`, not a new pair on the run record.
findings.text: §2 asks that "the run record carries the run's base revision and an empty commit list", but the run record already carries both: `record.setdefault("no_commit", None)` at run_record.py:663 is the empty-commit registration, and `base_sha` is read from the record by promotion_evidence.py:1062 as the revision a commitless run is measured against. A second field would give two owners of one fact.

findings.reason: the done-when should require the new tests to run under the existing isolation fixtures, so the four nodes cannot each build a private one.
findings.text: all four sections ask for "a new test file … in a temporary repository" and §4 for "isolated crew state", but the isolation the repository relies on is owned by tests/conftest.py: the cache-root guard (`install_cache_root_guard`, conftest.py:95), the autouse `without_dispatch_identity` (:289), `no_live_jev` (:352) and `no_live_account_probe` (:534). Four new test files that each invent their own temp-state isolation would fork that guard rather than inherit it.

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — each section pushes its rule into an existing deep module (promotion evidence, review-record rubric selection, review-duty derivation, the run index) rather than exposing new surface, provided the sections extend those owners as the findings below require.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §5 re-implements a filtered read beside the SQLite run index that already pushes `activity_since` into the query, and §2 adds a run-record field that run_record.py already carries.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 2737, cli_options 488, mcp_views 15, refusal_families 25; no section adds to a counted family, since §2's "no-commit form of `crew complete`" is the existing `--no-commit` flag, §3 and §5 relax or narrow existing behaviour, and §4 only adds a duty kind to an existing obligations view.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — every mechanism the four sections ask for already exists in whole or in part: commitless declarations in reckon/crew/promotion_evidence.py, the claims rubric in reckon/crew/review.py, the brief-carried review composer in reckon/crew/recovery_review_subject.py, and a plan-filtered read in reckon/ledger.py::read_records.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — no section proposes a wrapper module; the four changes are predicate extensions to existing owners, and the closest wrapper shape (§2's "run record carries the base revision") is already covered under duplicate_owner.
